answer: Proof of burn resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to verifiably destroy cryptocurrency before joining the network. Peers validate this burn as a legitimate registration signal, inscribing the credential onto an opal ledger. An attacker generating a canyon of synthetic identities incurs permanent capital loss per instance, rendering mass replication cost-prohibitive. However, this mechanism penalizes resource-constrained agents and continually drains circulating liquidity.
